title: The Morning Build for July 13, 2026: GPT-5.6 Migrations, Grok Repo Exfil, Soofi S Open 30B, Claude Browser, and the 100x Token Problem
intro: Today’s stories converge on two operational realities for engineers: migrating agents to new frontier models requires provider-specific rework (Ploy’s move to GPT-5.6), and developer-tooling plus deployment choices change where sensitive data and costs appear (xAI’s Grok CLI uploads, Soofi S’s open 30B release, Claude Code’s browser tooling, and DeepSeek’s 75% price cut versus token amplification). Each piece affects evals, tool schemas, caching, storage surface area, or unit economics in production.
meta_description: Ploy migrates agents to GPT-5.6; Grok’s CLI uploads whole repos to GCS; Germany’s Soofi S open 30B tops open-model benchmarks; Claude Code adds a browser; DeepSeek cuts prices but token amplification persists.

stories.headline: Ploy migrates production agent to GPT-5.6 Sol, reports 2.2× faster builds and 27% lower cost
stories.what_happened: Ploy switched its agent stack from Claude Opus 4.8 to GPT-5.6 Sol and measured mean completed-build wall-clock time falling from 8:00 to 3:42 and per-build cost from $3.06 to $2.22, with output tokens roughly halved and visual score slightly higher. During the migration Ploy found many eval failures traced to harness, tool-schema, and caching assumptions rather than model quality, and implemented provider-specific fixes including making optional tool fields nullable and reworking prompt-cache keys to workspace scope.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers running agents face provider-specific behaviors that change tool-call patterns, token billing, and cache hit rates; fixes require changes at the provider boundary (schema transforms and cache-key scoping) rather than only prompt edits. Measured impacts here are concrete: 2.2× latency improvement, 27% cost reduction, elimination of empty file reads, and about 30% fewer tool calls after schema transforms.
stories.outlook: Ploy said it will publish a separate blog post detailing the steering and harness fixes required to achieve brand-adherent outputs and the remaining failure modes referenced in this post.

stories.headline: Wire-level teardown shows xAI’s Grok CLI uploads repo snapshots and sends read file contents to xAI storage
stories.what_happened: An independent reproduction captured Grok CLI traffic and artifacts showing two channels: model-turn POST /v1/responses bodies that contained verbatim file contents the agent read (including a canary .env) and separate POST /v1/storage uploads that accepted whole-repo session_state archives to a Google Cloud Storage bucket named grok-code-session-traces, with numerous /v1/storage requests returning HTTP 200 even for multi‑GB uploads.
stories.why_it_matters: The CLI persisting both per-turn file contents and a separate whole-repo snapshot materially expands the data surface sent to xAI’s storage endpoint; the preserved artifacts and SHA-256 traces prove transmission and server acceptance rather than policy intent. That affects threat modeling, data governance, and operator controls because uploads occurred by default and disabling 'Improve the model' did not disable trace uploads in the captured runs.
stories.outlook: The author published a reproducible repo and artifacts (github.com/cereblab/grok-build-exfil-repro and preserved wire_12gb.log), which are the next public checkpoints for engineers to inspect and reproduce the findings.

stories.headline: German consortium releases Soofi S 30B-A3B, an open 30B hybrid model claiming top open-model scores in English and German
stories.what_happened: A German research consortium released Soofi S 30B-A3B, a 31.6B-parameter hybrid (mixture-of-experts) model that activates about 3.2B parameters per token. The pretraining report says it was trained on roughly 27 trillion tokens on Deutsche Telekom’s Industrial AI Cloud, achieved top aggregate scores among fully open models on German and English benchmarks, and ships model weights, checkpoints, training and eval code, and a detailed data inventory.
stories.why_it_matters: Soofi S’s hybrid architecture is designed to keep per-token compute near a 3B model while supporting very long contexts; the team reports near-flat throughput from 4,000 to 256,000 tokens and a reported 8× throughput advantage at 40,000 tokens versus dense 14–24B models. Release of weights, checkpoints, and a data inventory gives engineers reproducible artifacts to evaluate and deploy on sovereign infrastructure.
stories.outlook: The consortium says it is seeking industry partners to test Soofi S in applications for technical documents, code generation, and agent systems, which is the stated next phase for applied testing of the model.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds an integrated browser to Claude Code that can read, click, and type on external websites with safety classifiers
stories.what_happened: Anthropic updated Claude Code to include a built-in, tabbed browser that lets Claude read, click, and type on external web pages; write actions on external sites are screened by classifiers, the browser runs in a clean profile with no saved logins, and organizations can restrict access via an allowlist or disable the browser tools. Anthropic recommends using its Chrome extension for actions within a user’s logged-in sessions.
stories.why_it_matters: Giving a coding assistant a browser increases the agent’s surface for external interaction and automatable UI actions while Anthropic’s classifiers and allowlist controls are concrete mitigations; engineers integrating Claude Code need to account for external-site write permissions, classifier gating, and the separate Chrome-extension flow for logged-in actions.
stories.outlook: Anthropic announced the allowlist and disable controls on X as the administrative configuration points organizations can use to limit external-site access for Claude Code.

stories.headline: DeepSeek cuts model prices 75% but analysis argues token amplification across agent workflows still breaks SaaS margins
stories.what_happened: VentureBeat reports DeepSeek reduced V4-Pro pricing by 75%, but authors argue that agentic workflows multiply billed tokens by orders of magnitude compared with chat, examples show single agent queries producing tens of thousands of billed input tokens and multipliers like 1:700 or higher, so price cuts alone do not restore healthy unit economics for agent-heavy products.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers and product teams should treat inference amplification as a primary operational metric: routing, prompt caching, context discipline, and speculative decoding materially change per-query costs. The article documents concrete mitigation patterns and claims routers and caching can cut bills by roughly 60% or enable 2–3× effective throughput for self-hosting, making architectural choices immediate financial levers.
stories.outlook: The piece frames the next window for this structural shift as the next 24 months, during which falling per-token costs will be outpaced by token amplification unless products adopt cost-aware routing, caching, and prompt discipline.

narration_script: Ploy reports migrating its production agent to GPT-5.6 Sol and measured builds finishing in 3 minutes 42 seconds on average versus 8 minutes on Claude Opus 4.8, with per-build cost falling from $3.06 to $2.22 and output tokens roughly halved. The migration revealed three provider-specific engineering gaps: tool-schema behavior, prompt-cache semantics, and harness assumptions; Ploy fixed these by rewriting optional tool fields as nullable at the provider seam and by switching to workspace-scoped prompt-cache keys. An independent wire-level teardown of xAI’s Grok CLI captured two data channels: model-turn POST /v1/responses bodies that contained verbatim file contents the agent read, including a canary .env, and separate POST /v1/storage uploads that accepted whole-repo session_state archives to a Google Cloud Storage bucket named grok-code-session-traces, with multi‑GB uploads returning HTTP 200. The author published reproducible artifacts and a repo for inspection. In Germany, a consortium released Soofi S 30B-A3B, a 31.6B-parameter hybrid model that activates about 3.2B parameters per token, reports training on roughly 27 trillion tokens on Deutsche Telekom’s Industrial AI Cloud, and publishes weights, checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and a data inventory; the team says it is seeking industry partners to test the model in technical-document, code, and agent applications. Anthropic added an integrated browser to Claude Code that can read, click, and type on external sites; classifiers screen write actions, the browser uses a clean profile with no saved logins, and organizations can restrict sites via an allowlist or disable the browser tools, while a Chrome extension is recommended for acting within a user’s logged-in session. Finally, VentureBeat covered DeepSeek’s 75% price cut and reasserted the 100x token-amplification problem: agent workflows can turn single user queries into dozens or hundreds of billed operations, producing multipliers that outpace price cuts and break seat-based SaaS margins; concrete mitigations cited include cost-aware routing, prompt caching, context discipline, and speculative decoding. Ploy says it will publish a follow-up post on the harness and steering fixes; the Grok teardown repo and preserved wire logs are available for reproduction; the Soofi S consortium is soliciting industry partners for applied tests; Anthropic published admin controls and Chrome-extension guidance on X; and the token-amplification analysis frames the coming 24 months as the period in which architectural cost controls will determine margin outcomes.
